transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Most nights I end up eating until I feel uncomfortably full, even though I keep telling myself to stop earlier. It's really starting to bother me, so I figured it was time to talk to someone about it.
Do you feel a lack of control during these episodes of overeating, like you can't stop or skip it even if you wanted to?

Yeah, definitely. Once I get started, it honestly feels like something else takes over and I'm just shoveling food in while I'm flipping records or scrolling my phone. I'll keep telling myself "this is the last bite," but my hand just keeps going back to the bowl anyway.

How often do these episodes happen—do they occur at least once a week for several months? And after bingeing, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to prevent weight gain?

This has been happening at least a couple of nights every week for about four months now, ever since my wife's schedule changed. I don't do anything like throw up, take laxatives, or exercise to make up for it; instead, I just feel incredibly bloated and sluggish and end up crashing on the couch.
Do you often feel strong feelings of distress, shame, or guilt about these eating episodes right after they happen?

Yes, I definitely feel a lot of embarrassment and shame right after, and I always end up thinking, "you did it again." It's gotten to the point where I try to hide the behavior from my wife and eat when she's not around so she doesn't see how much I'm actually putting away.

Instead, the patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating with a clear sense of lack of control, occurring at least several times per week for the past four months, accompanied by marked distress and guilt, and absence of regular compensatory behaviors. These features are characteristic of F50.0 (Binge eating disorder). No other diagnosis fits as well at this time.
